case_scope_warning: Purposive cases are not a moratorium census. No nationwide count or geographic diffusion rate is inferred from their number.
key_findings: Gasoline concern has the largest January-to-July increase among the comparable named household-cost series; concern is not electoral-priority causality.
Data-center cost-benefit opposition rose nationally and in Wisconsin; all three measured partisan groups exceed 50%, while agreement on the same remedy is unproven.
Wisconsin's current-issue priority and turnout-screen results caution against assigning its race repricing to data centers.
State tariff, permitting, advisory and AI-compliance responses are economically distinct; federal gridlock does not eliminate them.
Healthcare concern remains high and remedies differ; no broad accelerating electoral-salience claim follows from this packet.

fed_background.claim: Monetary-policy decisions do not require approval by the president or Congress. Electoral outcomes can affect fiscal policy and appointments, but do not mechanically set the policy-rate path.

constraints: The joint contracts refer to organizational control in February 2027, not identical settlement rules to election-winner contracts.
Report quoted bid/ask and midpoint as observed; do not normalize the sum or multiply marginal probabilities.
The presidency is held fixed as a scenario convention, subject to constitutional succession.
A state governor's victory does not imply control of both chambers, local zoning or every regulator.
Markets resolving before January 2027 do not directly measure laws enacted by the incoming Congress.
Policy stage classifications are nominal categories, not ordinal enactment probabilities.
